author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list shows the first page when asked for a page below the first
summary: A request for the owner list with a page number below the first shows the first page and renders the normal listing, instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: a request for the owner list with page number 0 shows the first page of owners and the normal listing, not the error page
a request for the owner list with a negative page number shows the first page of owners and the normal listing
a page number below the first is treated as the first page whether or not a last-name search is applied
a request for the first page or any later page keeps the listing behavior it has today
non_goals: what a page number past the last page shows
what a page value that is not a number does
the veterinarian directory's handling of a page number below the first
notes: Covers Owner records edge case 4 in docs/prd.md. The two open non_goals are recorded as Open Questions in docs/prd.md; the owner's report named only page values below 1 on the owner list. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. No prd-autofix records existed to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory already covers this slice. docs/system-design.md Contracts names OwnerController as the owner of server-rendered owner search with paging, and the Overview records that request-level rules live in controllers rather than in a service layer. The fix is a page-number normalization inside that existing handler: no new type, package, pattern, or dependency, and OwnerRepository and the Thymeleaf view are untouched. Basis: read of OwnerController.java plus grep over docs/prd.md (no IDE oracle connected in this run, so the resolution rests on the file read, which is the weaker basis than a symbol query). The only docs edit this dispatch made is the Contracts row for OwnerController, which now carries REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 and names the normalization guarantee.
integration_points: OwnerController.processFindForm is the single entry point for GET /owners; the requested page reaches both the repository query and the ownersList view model through it
the ownersList view builds its page links from the currentPage model attribute set in addPaginationModel

patterns.description: findPaginatedForOwnersLastName converts the 1-based request page to a 0-based PageRequest; PageRequest.of rejects a negative index, and the resulting exception is what renders the error page today

processFindForm already normalizes its other request input (a null last name becomes the empty string) before use — normalize the page number in the same place, so the query and the view model see one value

risks.risk: normalizing inside the pagination helper alone leaves the raw value in the currentPage model attribute, so the listing renders page links from a page number that does not exist
risks.mitigation: normalize once at the handler entry, before both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel see the value

risks.risk: a clamp written as an inequality against the wrong bound silently changes the first-page and later-page behavior the fourth acceptance criterion protects
risks.mitigation: the existing OwnerControllerTests paging tests are the regression guard; keep them passing unchanged

notes: Non-goals stand as the prd-entry records them: a page past the last page, a non-numeric page value, and the veterinarian directory are all out of scope, and the vet listing's own pagination helper is deliberately left alone. This slice adds no row to Known Defects and removes none — the behavior was recorded as a PRD edge case, not as a confirmed defect. It does not narrow the two standing open questions about the missing service layer and the missing modularity test; a request-parameter normalization is a web-layer concern and belongs in the controller either way. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp a below-first owner-list page to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production file, one handler: eight added and two deleted lines inside OwnerController.processFindForm, a single module, no sensitive paths, and the two docs edits only restate the same normalization.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is computed once and threaded to both the repository query and the view model, so page 1 and above is arithmetically untouched and the two consumers cannot drift; no other caller of findPaginatedForOwnersLastName or addPaginationModel exists.
